FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Petroleum 
and their Related Products of Synthesis or Biological Origin Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 


The purpose of this standard is to provide manufacturers, vehicle operators, producers of hydrogen/natural gas/ 
hydrogen enriched compressed natural gas (HCNG), processors, fuelling station operators and others involved 
in handling and usage of the HCNG for automotive industry with the information on the fuel quality parameters. 
Some aspects of this standard may also be applicable for the use of HCNG in stationary combustion engines. 


Fuel meeting the requirements of this standard has to: 


a) provide for the safe operation of the vehicle and associated equipment needed for its fuelling and 
maintenance; 


b) protect the fuel system from the detrimental effects of corrosion, poisoning, and liquid or solid deposition; 
and 


c) provide satisfactory vehicle performance under any and all conditions of climate and driving demands. 


While preparing the specification for CNG a thorough analysis of product quality and ultimate vehicle performance 
were made. CNG fuel is now one of the mainstream clean fuel options implemented in India and there is a vast 
experience available in Indian market. 


HCNG fuel specification is being formulated for the first time. Hence, the test methods applicable for CNG 
specification are considered in this specification. No separate packing and marking clause has been included in 
this standard. Further, storage, compression and supply of the material shall be based on the instructions of the 
producers and automotive manufacturers using HCNG fuel. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17314 : 2019 


Indian Standard 


HYDROGEN ENRICHED COMPRESSED NATURAL 
GAS (HCNG) FOR AUTOMOTIVE PURPOSES — 
SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for the hydrogen enriched 
compressed natural gas (HCNG) fuel for automotive 
purposes. 


1.2 This standard pertains only to HCNG that enters 
the fuel containers on the vehicle. CNG delivered to 
a fuel refueling station tend to vary sometimes with 
the supply composition in the vehicles. Any alteration 
in this respect to meet the specification requirements 
of HCNG thus becomes the responsibility of both the 
supplier and the refueling station operator, who would 
determine the operating conditions accordingly.

3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions and those given in IS 15320 and ISO 14532 
shall apply. 


3.1 CNG — is a compressed natural gas meeting the 
requirement of IS 15958. 


3.2 Hydrogen — Hydrogen that has been produced to 
gaseous form and meeting the requirements of type I of 
IS 16061(Part 1)/ISO 14687-1. 


4 REQUIREMENTS 


4.1 HCNG shall be free from liquids over the entire 
range of temperatures and pressures encountered in the 
storage and dispensing system, fuel containers, engine 
and fuel system. 


4.2 The HCNG fuel shall be technically free from 
particulate matter, such as, dust, dirt and mist. 
NOTE — It is essential to keep debris out of the vehicle 
containers. For this purpose, it is recommended at least a 5 um 


filter is used in the fuel line feeding the vehicle container. This 
usage constitutes a specification for debris control. 


IS 17314 : 2019 


4.3 Odour 


HCNG delivered to any natural gas vehicle shall be 
odorized similar to a level found in the local distribution 
(see IS 15319). 


4.4 HCNG shall be free of methanol/glycol. 


4.5 The material shall also comply with the requirements 
given in column3 of Table 1. 


5 SUPPLY OF HCNG 


5.1 HCNG shall be stored and supplied in accordance 
with the relevant regulatory provisions of PNGRB 
and instructions given by the automotive vehicle 
manufacturers. 


5.2 Receipt of natural gas through pipelines by the retail 
outlet, storage, compression and dispensing shall be 
done in accordance with relevant regulatory provisions 
of PNGRB the instructions given by the gas suppliers. 


6 SAMPLING 


The representative samples shall be drawn as prescribed 
in IS 15125. 


7 QUALITY OF REAGENTS 
Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled 
water shall be used in tests (see IS 1070). 


NOTE — Pure chemicals shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities which affect the result of the analysis. 


Table 1 Requirements for Hydrogen enriched Compressed Natural Gas 
for Automotive Purposes 


( Clause 4.5 ) 


SI No. Characteristic Requirement Test Method 

(1) 2 6) (4) 

i) Hydrogen (percent volume) 18.0 + 1.0 IS 15130 (Part 3) 

ii) Methane (percent volume), Min 72.0 

iii) Other hydrocarbons (percent volume) IS 15130 (Part 3) 
a) Ethane, Max 6.0 
b) C, and higher HC, Max 3.0 
c) C, and higher HC, Max 0.5 
d) Total unsaturated HC, Max 0.5 

iv) Impurities 
a) Water content, mg/m’, Max 5.0 IS 15641 (Part 2) 
b) Total sulphur’, mg/m3, Max 20 ASTM D3246 
c) Oxygen, percent volume, Max 0.5 IS 15130 (Part 3) 
d) Carbon dioxide and nitrogen, percent volume, Max 3.5 IS 15130 (Part 3) 
e) Carbon monoxide, percent mole, Max 0.1 IS 15130 (Part 3) 


D Total sulphur includes the sulphur content of odorant

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part ofthese publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: PCD 03 (14137).
